subject: Post-demo: hosted suitability — network egress, region, and trial cadence
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>, Mark Chu <mark.chu@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: hosted suitability — network egress, region, and trial cadence

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying items so we can scope the right onramp (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) and get your pilot scheduled.

What we covered (high level):
- Demonstration of standard Hosted API endpoints (generation + chat + embeddings) and token accounting.
- Showed region selection and how model variants can be routed for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Walked through prefix/KV caching benefits for multi-turn flows.

Open clarifications from our side to help recommend the deployment path:
1) Data residency & network: Do you need traffic to stay within a VPC (peer) or is regional hosting (e.g., us-west-2) sufficient? Our Hosted offering does not do VPC peering — Private deployment supports VPC/on-prem.
2) Expected throughput profile: please confirm average and peak RPS and average tokens per request (sample estimate you mentioned ~1k tokens / request).
3) SLA and compliance: you mentioned SOC2 + audit logs are required for procurement — can you confirm whether standard SOC2 plus API audit trails suffice, or do you need a customer-controlled KMS/HSM?
4) Trial scope: would you prefer a short, focused 2-week sandbox with capped rate limits and sample production traffic, or a longer proof-of-concept with a dedicated capacity estimate?

Proposed next steps:
- If you can confirm (1)-(3) above, we’ll spin up a hosted sandbox with an allow-listed IP range and a default rate policy (we typically start with 60 requests/minute and 500k tokens/day as a conservative sandbox — configurable).
- Marissa will share the Hosted Quickstart Playbook and an IP allowlist CSV to make onboarding fast.
- We can set a 30-minute ops preflight to configure prefix caching, expected sequence length, and SLOs.

Attachments: Hosted-Quickstart-Playbook.pdf (playbook + checklist)

Thanks — I’ll wait for the three clarifications and a preferred pilot start date.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chu <mark.chu@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted suitability — network egress, region, and trial cadence

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A few quick answers and follow-ups from our side:
- Residency: we prefer traffic to stay in our cloud region (us-west-2). VPC peering would be ideal but not mandatory for an initial pilot; procurement will push for it if we go to production.
- Throughput: our initial pilot window will hit ~20 RPS average during business hours with spikes up to ~200 RPS for short bursts.
- Tokens: confirmed ~1k tokens/request average for the flows we demonstrated; peak daily token budget for the pilot ~200k tokens.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II is required. Audit logs are necessary; KMS-managed keys would be a nice-to-have but not mandatory for the pilot.

Two asks: can Hosted support IP allowlisting + regional data residency for the pilot? Also, please send estimated pricing for Dedicated capacity as a side-by-side (we want to understand TCO if we need VPC peering later).

Samira
Samira Khan | Head of Integrations, FinLytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted suitability — network egress, region, and trial cadence

Hi Samira — great questions. Quick answers + what I’m attaching.

1) IP allowlisting + regional residency: yes — for Hosted we can enforce an IP allowlist and pin your sandbox to us-west-2 so data remains in-region. Note: Hosted does not support VPC peering or private-link for customer VPCs; that capability is available if you move to Private deployment.

2) Rate limits & burst: sandbox defaults are conservative — 60 req/min with automatic short-window burst smoothing. For your pilot (20 avg / 200 peak) we recommend starting with a throttled sandbox at 120 req/min with a 1-minute token bucket sized to 500k tokens/day and a burst allowance of 2x for short spikes. We can tune after observing 48 hours of traffic.

3) Audit logs / SOC2: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. Hosted includes API audit trails; if you need a dedicated KMS we can discuss Private deployment or an enterprise add-on.

4) KV cache & long-context: prefix caching will significantly reduce per-token cost for multi-turn flows; for ~1k token requests, we expect 20-40% token savings depending on repetition. We’ll include cache recommendations in the playbook.

Attachments: Hosted-Quickstart-Playbook.pdf (checklist + ops runbook), IP-allowlist-template.csv (small sample to paste into your firewall)

Next steps I’ll action:
- Share a Hosted sandbox access token + ephemeral endpoint (Trial-Access-Link) once you confirm pilot start date.
- Put together a short Dedicated TCO sheet so you can compare if VPC peering is a hard requirement later.

Propose a 30-minute ops preflight on Thu Mar 29 at 9:30am PT — does that work?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Product Specialist, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Chu <mark.chu@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted suitability — network egress, region, and trial cadence

Thanks Marissa — that’s clear and promising. Two quick clarifications before Thu:
- Burst handling: you propose 2x burst allowance — does that mean short spikes to 400 RPS will be allowed (and then smoothed)? We need guarantees that spikes won’t be dropped entirely.
- Token accounting: will the pilot show per-request token breakdown (input/output), and is there a way to emit per-request names/trace ids in audit logs? That’s important for our observability.

If we get both answers we’re comfortable moving forward with Thu preflight and a pilot start on Mon Apr 2.

Samira
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Mark Chu <mark.chu@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted suitability — network egress, region, and trial cadence

Samira — short answers and action items.

- Burst: Hosted sandbox will allow short bursts above the configured steady-state limit; bursts are smoothed by a token-bucket policy rather than dropped immediately. For the pilot we will configure a 2x short-burst window and monitor. If we see sustained overage we’ll throttle gracefully and surface 429s with a Retry-After header so your client can exponential-backoff.

- Token accounting & audit logs: yes — the sandbox includes per-request token breakdown (input/output) visible in the Console and emitted to the audit log. We can configure the audit trail to capture a trace_id and request metadata; we do not log raw user content by default for retention/compliance reasons, but you can enable stricter logging in Private deployments.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa: share sandbox token + Trial-Access-Link, Hosted Quickstart playbook, and IP-allowlist template (done).
- Vivek: follow up with a draft Dedicated TCO and a short note on KMS options (Vivek will join Thu preflight).
- Samira/FinLytics: confirm pilot start date (you suggested Mon Apr 2) and provide the IP ranges you’ll allowlist.

I’ll send a calendar invite for Thu 9:30am PT and include a short agenda (preflight + config). Looking forward to the pilot.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
